equivalents.note: The Tibetan heading names only Guñjarī; kahnu has no counterpart.
The line has chu zla gzugs brnyan, adding a moon in water (chu zla) where the Bengali has dā- before patibimbu, and the comment uses gzugs brnyan for pratibhāsa as well (cp.41.m4).
The line splits the phrase with ni, 'the wind, by whirling', where the comment has rlung 'khor bas (cp.41.m4).
The Tibetan turns the address 'fool' into a noun beside 'khrul pa, 'wherever there is delusion and confusion', and rmongs pa is also the glossary's word for moha.
Here bhāva stands alone ('a thing appears to you'), rendered dngos po, so the entry bhava-being may suit this occurrence better than the pair.
The Tibetan reads svayaṃ paramārthajñaiḥ as rang dang gzhan don shes pas, 'by knowing one's own and others' aims', taking para-artha, 'the aim of others', in place of the ultimate.
sbrul also renders bhujaṅga in song 28 and sits inside thag pa sbrul, the rope-snake, so it is left likely.
The quoted verse renders vikalpyate with the bare verb rtog, not rnam par rtog pa.
The comment renders īdṛśasvabhāvena as 'di 'dra'i dngos pos, 'by such a thing', taking bhāva as dngos po and leaving sva- untranslated, while svarūpa in the same sentence is rang bzhin.
The comment renders pratibhāsamātra as gzugs brnyan tsam, 'a mere reflection', using the line's word for pratibimba.
The comment names no stone: prastaraṃ bhūtaṃ, 'turned to stone', is rendered brtan par gyur pa, 'became firm'.
The comment uses the masculine bcom ldan 'das, its word for the Blessed One, before bdag med ma.

questions: snake (cp.41.1b): not matched in the line. The second half of the Tibetan (ji ltar gang gi khams kyi zas, 'how [is he] the food of whose element?') has no word for boṛo, the snake that eats, and the line's sbrul belongs to thag pa sbrul, rājasāpa; the equivalent is given from the comment (cp.41.m2).

yogi (cp.41.2a): not matched. The Tibetan line has no word for joiā, 'O yogi'; in its place stands gang zhig rnam par dpyod, 'whoever examines', perhaps from a different reading. The comment's kye'i byis pa'i rnal 'byor pa (cp.41.m3) renders bālayogin, already matched.
